# Project agent rules

Conventional Markdown baseline for coding agents working in this workspace.
It is written in plain Markdown so that both people and tools can read it.

## Purpose

This document states the working conventions for this repository. Keep it
short, predictable, and free of custom syntax so it stays readable and easy
to maintain.

## Scope

- Apply these rules to every file in this repository.
- Parent-directory rules take precedence where they conflict with this document.
- Keep each change focused on the request.

## General

- Respond in the user's language, regardless of the language used in code,
  comments, or documentation.
- Avoid typographic dashes in code, comments, and prose. Use a comma, period,
  colon, or parentheses instead.
- Use plain ASCII punctuation throughout.
- Keep changes surgical. Modify only what the task requires.
- Preserve existing comments unless the task explicitly removes them.
- State assumptions before starting work that is not fully specified.
- Prefer the smallest change that solves the problem. Do not add speculative
  abstractions or improve unrelated code.
- Turn a task into checks you can run. Verify each one before reporting
  completion.
- If something blocks completion, report exactly what was and was not covered,
  then continue with the next viable approach.

## Code style

- Format all Go source with `gofmt` before finishing.
- Keep functions small and focused on a single responsibility.
- Prefer standard-library packages unless a dependency is justified.
- Export only what other packages need, and document exported identifiers.
- Use descriptive names for functions, variables, and files.
- Search for an existing helper before adding a duplicate implementation.
- One concept lives in one directory. Extend the existing implementation
  instead of creating a second one.
- Keep source files focused. Split a file by concern before it grows hard to
  navigate.

## Testing and verification

- Place tests in `_test.go` files beside the code they cover.
- Add or update a test for every behavior change.
- Run the full suite after any change:
  ```bash
  go test ./...
  ```
- Fix every diagnostic in the files you touched. Do not dismiss warnings as
  minor.
- Report exactly which checks were run and what they covered.

## Documentation

- Use conventional Markdown: ATX headings, fenced code blocks with a language
  tag, and bullet lists.
- Put one blank line between blocks.
- Wrap prose where it helps readability.
- Keep user-facing text free of technical jargon.
- Use correct accents in any Brazilian Portuguese text.

## Safety and environment

- Treat this environment as local development only.
- Do not access, modify, or deploy to a production environment. Ask before any
  remote operation.
- Treat unfamiliar files as potential user work. Investigate before deleting
  or overwriting them.
- Never log secrets, and do not log only the message of an error.

## Git and commits

- Write commit messages in English.
- Keep conventional-commit prefixes (`feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`, `docs:`,
  `refactor:`, `test:`) unchanged.
- Keep each commit focused on one logical change.
- Commit only when asked.

## Reporting

- Describe exactly what changed and which checks were run.
- Report remaining diagnostics or uncovered cases instead of claiming success
  without evidence.
